title: Marina Parrondo Lombardía
text:
I develop and apply molecular and genomic tools to address marine conservation and fisheries-management challenges, particularly in species for which the biological information needed for effective management remains limited.
My research spans population genetics, molecular identification, and biodiversity monitoring in marine invertebrates. At Dalhousie University, I am extending this work into population genomics and movement ecology, integrating low-coverage whole-genome sequencing with acoustic telemetry in Atlantic cod.
About me · Explore my research

title: About
text:
I am a marine biologist developing molecular and genomic approaches to support marine conservation and sustainable fisheries management.
A common thread throughout my research has been the need to build biological knowledge for species and ecosystems that remain poorly characterized. I have focused particularly on commercially and ecologically important marine invertebrates, for which genetic baselines, curated molecular reference libraries, and genome-wide resources are often limited.
During my PhD, I developed population-genetic baselines for exploited marine invertebrates and investigated how genetic information could support sustainable fisheries management.
During my first postdoctoral fellowship, I expanded this perspective from individual species to vulnerable marine ecosystems. My work focused on developing integrative taxonomic and DNA-barcoding resources to support future environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring.

title: About
text:
Current position
In April 2025, I joined Daniel Ruzzante’s laboratory at Dalhousie University in Nova Scotia, Canada, as a Postdoctoral Fellow working on the Northern Cod Acoustic Tracking (NCAT) project.
Within NCAT, I integrate low-coverage whole-genome sequencing with acoustic telemetry to investigate relationships between genomic variation and individual movement patterns in Atlantic cod.
This position builds on my experience with microsatellite and mitochondrial datasets while extending my expertise into genome-wide analyses, the computational management of large sequencing datasets, and the analysis of animal movement and spatial connectivity.

title: About
text:
Looking ahead
My move to Atlantic cod was a deliberate step towards learning in a system with established genomic resources and acoustic-telemetry infrastructure.
My long-term aim is to adapt and transfer these approaches to data-poor marine invertebrates, connecting genomic and ecological information to address conservation and fisheries-management needs.

title: Research
text: My research connects molecular identification, population genetics, genomics, and movement ecology to address questions relevant to marine conservation and fisheries management.

title: Research
text:
Population genetics for fisheries management
Reliable genetic baselines are essential for investigating population structure and connectivity in exploited marine species.
During my PhD, I developed population-genetic baselines for marine invertebrates and explored how this information could contribute to sustainable fisheries management.

title: Research
section: Molecular reference resources for biodiversity monitoring
text:
Molecular reference resources for biodiversity monitoring
Molecular monitoring depends on reliable links between DNA sequences and taxonomic identities.
During my first postdoctoral fellowship, I worked on integrative taxonomic and DNA-barcoding resources for vulnerable marine ecosystems, helping establish the reference information needed for future environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring.

title: Research
section: Linking genomic variation and movement in Atlantic cod
text:
Linking genomic variation and movement in Atlantic cod
At Dalhousie University, I work on the Northern Cod Acoustic Tracking (NCAT) project in Daniel Ruzzante’s laboratory.
I integrate low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (lcWGS) with acoustic telemetry to investigate relationships between genomic variation and individual movement patterns in Atlantic cod.
This work brings together population-genomic analyses, the management of large sequencing datasets, and the interpretation of movement and spatial connectivity data.

title: Research
text:
A long-term perspective
Across these research areas, my goal is to strengthen the biological evidence available for marine species with limited genomic resources.
By developing expertise in a comparatively data-rich system, I aim to identify approaches that can ultimately be adapted to marine invertebrates and other data-poor systems.
